title: A Story with a Twist
paragraphs: It was the afternoon of Amir's final exam of the semester, and everything had gone wrong before he even reached the university. He had woken up forty minutes late because he had forgotten to set his alarm the night before. He had dressed in four minutes, eaten nothing, and run to the bus stop — only to discover that the bus had already left. He had stood at the empty stop in the grey morning air and felt, for a long moment, completely defeated.

He called a taxi. The taxi driver, a silent man named Bakyt, drove in what seemed to Amir like slow motion. They were stuck behind a vehicle that had broken down in the middle of the road. Amir checked the time constantly. He had been in Uralsk for eight months by then and had never, not once, been late to anything. The idea of missing the exam felt physically impossible — and yet, here he was.

Bakyt said nothing for most of the journey. Then, five minutes from the university, he switched off the meter and said: "I'm not going to charge you for the wait. It wasn't your fault." Amir looked at the back of his head, surprised. He had not expected this. He said thank you, and meant it more than he had meant any thank you in a long time.

He arrived at the exam room with two minutes to spare. His professor, Dr. Seitkali, raised an eyebrow as he walked in. Amir took his seat, took a breath, and started writing. The exam, which he had been preparing for every evening for two weeks, went better than he had expected. He knew all the answers. He had done the work. Whatever had happened that morning — the alarm, the bus, the broken-down car — had not been enough to stop him.

Afterwards, in the corridor, he told Kamila what had happened. She listened and then said: "Do you think Bakyt does that often? Turns off the meter for people who are having a bad day?" Amir thought about it. "Maybe," he said. "Or maybe he just had a feeling that morning." Kamila smiled. "Either way," she said, "he turned your day around." Amir nodded. A stranger who had offered a small kindness at exactly the right moment. The city, which had felt hostile that morning, suddenly felt different.

That evening, Amir wrote about it in his notebook. He wrote: "I had expected the worst day of the semester, and then one small thing changed everything. A man I had never met, who owed me nothing, decided to be kind. And somehow, that was enough." He underlined the last sentence. He did not know why exactly. But it felt important.

He has not forgotten it. Sometimes, when things go wrong — when he has woken up late, missed a deadline, made a mistake — he thinks about Bakyt. And about the meter. And about the space that kindness makes in a day that had seemed to have no space left at all.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: You won't believe what happened this morning before the exam.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: What? You look shaken. Are you OK?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I overslept, missed the bus, got stuck in traffic — and then the taxi driver turned off the meter for me.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: He just turned it off? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: He said it wasn't my fault. I hadn't done anything to deserve it. He just did.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Do you think he does that regularly?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I don't know. But I had been so stressed all morning, and that one thing made everything feel manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's the power of small kindnesses. They arrive exactly when you need them.

keyPhrases.context: "Everything had gone wrong before he even reached the university." — happened before a past event.
"He had forgotten to set his alarm the night before." — before waking up late.
"He had been preparing for every evening for two weeks." — before the exam.
"Two minutes to spare." = two minutes of extra time; not late.
"He turned your day around." = changed how the day felt.
"Better than he had expected." — what he expected before the exam started.
"Who owed me nothing." = was not obliged to help me.
"He underlined the last sentence." = drew a line under it to mark importance.

vocab.definition: feeling that you have lost or failed; without hope
vocab.example: "He felt completely defeated." — lost and hopeless at the bus stop.
"He checked the time constantly." — again and again, without stopping.

vocab.definition: extra beyond what is needed; "to spare" = available
vocab.example: "He arrived with two minutes to spare." — two extra minutes.
"The city, which had felt hostile that morning, suddenly felt different."

vocab.definition: a device in a taxi that measures the fare to be paid
vocab.example: "He switched off the meter." — stopped charging for the waiting time.

vocab.definition: a long narrow passage inside a building
vocab.example: "In the corridor, he told Kamila what had happened."

vocab.definition: to draw a line under text; to emphasise something
vocab.example: "He underlined the last sentence." — marked it as important.

vocab.definition: the latest time by which something must be done
vocab.example: "When he has missed a deadline." — failed to complete by the required time.
